title: Best Electric Grills UK
short: Six electric tabletop grills compared on cooking results, cleaning and family-sized capacity, from a £33 budget model to a £230 sensor-controlled grill.
intro: An electric grill funnels fat away from meat as it cooks, sears in juices for flavour, and is faster and cheaper to run than heating a full oven. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup, where each grill cooked chicken breasts, steak and vegetables of a consistent thickness, checked for drying or burning and timed for how long each item took. Testers also made paninis where a grill doubled as a sandwich press, noted heat-up time, presets and variable temperature options, and assessed cooking area, storage and how easy each grill was to clean. Prices are as reviewed.

products.name: Optigrill Elite
products.best_for: Anyone who wants a sensor-guided grill that adapts to food thickness
products.key_spec: 12 programmes plus manual and frozen modes, removable dishwasher-safe plates, 36.3 x 34.1 x 18cm
products.summary: Expert Reviews' Best Buy: an intelligent health grill with a sensor that adjusts grilling time to food thickness, 12 programmes from bacon to burgers, a manual mode, cooking from frozen, and a 'refill' option to cook batches without resetting. In testing it slightly over-predicted cooking time for thick chicken breasts and under-predicted a vegetable programme, but cooked steak to the perfect rareness manually. Preheating takes 4 to 7 minutes, and there's no cancel button, so you must remove food or unplug it to reset a programme.
pros: Sensor adjusts grilling time to food thickness
12 programmes, manual mode and grill-from-frozen option
Robust build quality with a deep drip tray
cons: No cancel button to switch between programmes
Predicted cooking times weren't always accurate

products.name: Cosmos Non-Stick Coated Health Grill
products.best_for: Solo households or light lunches on a tight budget and in a small kitchen
products.key_spec: Automatic temperature (no control), fixed plates, 26 x 16cm cooking surface, 30.1 x 26.7 x 12.9cm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found it performed excellently despite basic 'automatic' temperature adjustment and no manual control: plates heated quickly and cooked chicken breasts juicy with good searing, with plenty of liquid draining into the drip tray. Asparagus took much longer, presumably because the grill self-adjusted to a lower temperature with no indication of when. The compact cooking surface only fits two chicken breasts or a bunch of asparagus, not both, and it doesn't fold flat, but the fixed non-stick plates were easy to wipe clean.
pros: Heats up quickly and cooks chicken juicy with good searing
Fixed plates are easy to clean
cons: No temperature control, asparagus took much longer to cook
Limited grilling space, doesn't fold flat
products.search: Salter Cosmos Non-Stick Coated Health Grill

products.name: Immersa Grill
products.best_for: Simple, fast grilling with the easiest possible clean-up
products.key_spec: Single temperature, removable control panel, grill plates and drip tray dishwasher-safe, 27.8 x 30.8 x 10.7cm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found straightforward, hassle-free grilling at a reasonable price. Its removable control panel is the standout feature, letting the rest of the grill go straight into the dishwasher or sink after use. It reached operating temperature in a speedy four minutes and produced nicely grilled steaks, chicken breasts and vegetables with good char lines and moist interiors. It operates at a single temperature with no extra settings, and comes in Individual and larger Family sizes.
pros: Removable control panel makes the grill fully washable
Non-stick, smokeless plates let fat drip away
Reaches operating temperature in four minutes
cons: Single temperature with no extra settings or modes

products.name: Griddle and Grill
products.best_for: Feeding a family, with the flexibility of a sandwich press, health grill or hot plate
products.key_spec: Folds flat to a 60 x 48cm surface, 100°C to 240°C variable temperature, floating hinge, 30-minute timer
products.summary: Expert Reviews found it heated up quickly, cooking steak to medium-rare and corn on the cob without burning the exterior. Folded flat it creates a large 60 x 48cm cooking surface, great for a family meal, or you can use just one plate for smaller portions. A floating hinge accommodates thicker foods like large chicken legs, and a 30-minute timer helps you step away, though it doesn't switch the appliance off automatically. The heavy upper plate squashed a test sandwich slightly, and there's no obvious storage for the second set of plates.
pros: Folds flat to a large 60 x 48cm surface, great for families
Flexible temperature range from slow cooking to searing meat
cons: Heavy upper plate squashed a test sandwich slightly
No obvious storage for the second set of plates
Timer doesn't switch the appliance off

products.name: Design BBQ Advanced Smart
products.best_for: Anyone who wants precise doneness settings for steak without the guesswork
products.key_spec: 6 programmes including 4 steak doneness levels, independently controlled plates, two 25 x 28cm grilling areas when flat
products.summary: Expert Reviews found programmes for poultry, burgers, paninis, fish, sandwiches, sausages and steak (with four doneness options from rare to well-done) that take much of the guesswork out of grilling. Heating elements built into the removable plates heat up fast, the plates can be independently controlled to different temperatures, and an adjustable upper lid stops food being squashed. Chicken breasts emerged beautifully grilled and juicy in testing, though vegetables became a bit singed with no vegetable preset, and programmes can only be set with the grill closed.
pros: Four steak doneness settings take out the guesswork
Independently controlled plates heat up fast
Adjustable lid height and a floating hinge
cons: No vegetable preset, veg can get singed
Programmes can only be set when the grill is closed

products.name: 25810 Medium Fit Grill
products.best_for: Occasional users who want a decent-sized grill without spending much
products.key_spec: Single temperature, fixed plates, 31 x 16.5cm cooking surface, adjustable foot for fat run-off, 33.3 x 27.5 x 7.7cm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found it large enough for a couple of whole meals, stores vertically to save space, and heats to 230°C in around six minutes thanks to fixed plates. An adjustable foot tips it forward so fat runs away, or it can sit flat. It cooked meat and vegetables without issue in testing, though cheese in a panini took a while to melt, and as a single-temperature machine some foods need closer monitoring to avoid burning. The fixed non-stick plates are easiest wiped down while still warm.
pros: Large enough for a couple of whole meals
Heats to 230°C in around six minutes
cons: Single temperature, needs closer monitoring to avoid burning
Fixed plates are a bit of a chore to clean

guide.a: Removable plates, like on the Tefal Optigrill Elite and Cuisinart, can go straight in the dishwasher for easier cleaning. Fixed plates, as on the Salter Cosmos and both George Foreman models here, heat up faster and tend to be cheaper, but need wiping in place; Expert Reviews found this easiest done while the grill is still warm.

guide.q: Do I need variable temperature or programmes?
guide.a: A single-temperature grill like the George Foreman models works well for meat but can be too hot for delicate fish or vegetables. If you cook a range of foods, a model with programmes, like the Tefal Optigrill Elite or Gastroback Design BBQ, or simple variable temperature like the Cuisinart, gives more control.

guide.q: How much cooking area do I need?
guide.a: For a couple of items at a time, a compact grill like the Salter Cosmos or George Foreman Immersa is enough. For a full family meal, look for one that folds flat to a larger surface, like the Cuisinart (60 x 48cm) or Gastroback (two 25 x 28cm areas).

guide.q: What is a floating hinge and why does it matter?
guide.a: A floating hinge lets the top plate tilt to match the thickness of what you're cooking, rather than being fixed at one angle like a basic sandwich press. Expert Reviews highlights this on the Cuisinart and Gastroback grills, helping thicker foods like chicken legs cook evenly without being squashed.
